> Moon Info

Crew: ?

CONDITION: Intact, aged, few components destroyed.

Contains several hazardous substances and Fauna.

> Environment

> Moon Exclusive Content

The player's clock is hidden while on ResearcherxB. However, time progresses at its normal speed. ResearcherxB's exterior will also have its lights turned off if the power in the interior is turned off.

In the main corridor to the left after exiting the ship, there are several doors the player can open or shut from that side. At the end of this corridor is a door that requires a keycard to open, which "Cavil's keycard" is a guaranteed scrap spawn within the interior. Opening this door leads to a room covered in white mold, and similarly has the mold spikes found on the exterior of Vindict. Five random scrap from ResearcherxB's Loot Table is guaranteed to spawn on a table in this room. Two terminals can also be interacted with in this room and the one next to the left ship lever will unlock Carnate.

Additionally, a panel immediately to the right can be moved to reveal eight differently colored wires and two valves. Players must cut the colored wires that have a red light above them at one or two panels. One is on the wall in the big room to the left of the main corridor and the other is on the wall next to a regular door to the left of the main entrance. Cutting a wrong wire will deal 100 damage to the player. Afterwards, players must return to the original panel and repeatedly interact with the valves.

Finally, players can decide to overload ResearcherxB by interacting with the left ship lever in this room after completing the above puzzle. If pulled, players will receive a warning that the ship will explode in 30 seconds. The autopilot will leave after these 30 seconds and all players still on the exterior or in the interior will be abandoned. Players can still route to ResearcherxB afterward, but there will be nothing there other than the debris floating in space. This change is permanent on that save file, will prevent ResearcherxB from crash landing onto and infecting Trite, and cause debris from ResearcherxB to fall randomly onto the exteriors of some moons.

> Progression

Unlocked By

Setting up a Triangulation Device on Vindict and another six random moons as prompted. This must be accomplished within a random number of days of in-game time, as ResearcherxB can no longer be located and will begin to crash onto Trite otherwise. This change is permanent on that save file. Players can receive at least three distress signals from the ship while on a moon and each signal warns players of how many days are remaining. Being fired will reset triangulation progress but will not affect the countdown.

Triangulation Devices can be crafted on Galetry or Gratar. Additionally, there is a chance to find a device on the exteriors of Glace, Selector, Trite, and Vindict on caches of scrap that can be collected once per save file. Excluding the "Recovery order", this scrap is randomized per landing and players can reroll what scrap is there by not getting too close to the cache.

Unlocks

Carnate: Interact with the terminal past the keycard door and to the left of the ship lever. If ResearcherxB crashes or is blown up before interacting with the terminal, Carnate will be inaccessible on that save file.

> Lore

Researcher Logs

Success

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 16
—----------------------- 10:36 - Lab

S. Dent: I think that’s it. I think we’ve got it. This will be perfect when it’s merged with the main compound.
C. Darter: Yeah.. that’s great.
S. Dent: Is something wrong? I thought you’d be celebrating.
C. Darter: I don’t think we’re doing the right thing.
S. Dent: How so? We’re helping people. If not for the Triton Empire we’re saving people’s lives with this.
S. Dent: Are we not? Cavil?
C. Darter: They uh.. You aren’t allowed to know but it’s likely not for the purpose you’ve been led to believe.
S. Dent: What do you mean? This is medicine, it will protect people.
C. Darter: Yes but. Not the people you might think.
S. Dent: Well.. Go on.
C. Darter: This is part of Project Mycete. A project where they’re attempting to make enhanced soldiers by stuffing them with experimental drugs.
S. Dent: What.
C. Darter: And.. not only that but out there people are being slaughtered, tortured and murdered in pursuit of people fit for the procedure.
S. Dent: WHAT.
S. Dent: All this time. I have been working for a lie. Harming these poor creatures. Just so we have a small step up in this conquest??.
C. Darter: .. Basically.
S. Dent: Why didn’t you tell me?
C. Darter: I mean, they will likely have me repurposed when they discover I have now leaked this information.. It’s more of an execution than a repurpose.
S. Dent: Right. So. What now?. Do we leave? Do we burn it all? Tell me.
C. Darter: I need time to think. I don’t want to hand Sol this research. We’ll talk about this tomorrow. Pretend like none of this happened.
S. Dent: Yeah. Okay. Simple. I’ll just simply pretend like I haven’t spent the past two and half weeks risking my life for a lie.
C. Darter: I mean it.
—----------------------- 16:13 - Office

J. Charter: Sarah? Are you okay?
S. Dent: I’m fine.
J. Charter: The tears running down your face say otherwise. Did something happen?
S. Dent: I would prefer not to talk about it.
J. Charter: Something personal?
S. Dent: Yea.
J. Charter: I see.. If something is up you can talk to me about it, it’s okay.
S. Dent: Wouldn’t want it to be a detriment to the mission would you.
J. Charter: What?
S. Dent: No I mean. I’m sorry. I don’t know where that came from. It’s just hard. I’m not sure if I can take much more of it.
J. Charter: It’s okay, I get it.
S. Dent: Did Cavil send you?
J. Charter: No he didn’t.
S. Dent: What made you come here?
J. Charter: Well you’ve seemed a bit down today. It’s important that everyone on this crew feels okay. And I also care.. about.. you. I mean..
S. Dent: Thank you, I really appreciate it. There’s just.. Maybe I miss home and it’s wearing me down.
J. Charter: That makes sense. I can’t say I don’t miss it back there. Sooner or later we’ll be back. We just have to complete our mission. We’ll be okay.
S. Dent: Yeah. Thank you, really.

Execution

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 17 
—----------------------- 18:56 - Maintenance tunnel

C. Darter: Hopefully nobody can hear us down here.
S. Dent: Hope so too. Have you got an idea?
C. Darter: I have a plan. It will be hairy.
S. Dent: Alright. Can’t be worse than whatever they’re doing out there.
C. Darter: It’s a two part plan. We have to destroy the autopilot. And manually route it somewhere else so they won’t be able to find it. I wrote the coordinates on this note. Send this ship here.
S. Dent: Uhm. Okay. What will you do?
C. Darter: I’ll make sure they won’t be able to track the ship anymore and prepare the escape pod.
S. Dent: What about Julian? We tell him right?
C. Darter: It’s better if we don’t. He’s loyal to the Triton Empire. I don’t trust him to betray that.
S. Dent: Well we can’t just leave him. Maybe he’ll listen to me.
C. Darter: It’d be best not to try. He might sound the alarm.
S. Dent: I won’t leave him.
C. Darter: If you can convince him to join us in the escape pod he can come with. But only after you’ve done your part.
S. Dent: Right, If this is another lie I’ll kill you.
C. Darter: I promise.
S. Dent: When do we start?
C. Darter: 22:00. I’ll have the escape pod ready by 23:30. Be there.
S. Dent: Okay.
C. Darter: I have some digging to do. Good luck.
S. Dent: You too.

—----------------------- 22:24 - Security office

J. Charter: The fuck.

—----------------------- 22:38 - Cockpit

J. Charter: Who’s there? Sarah?
S. Dent: Julian?
J. Charter: What are you doing? Did you mess with the autopilot?
S. Dent: I can explain.
J. Charter: Is this an order? Why are you doing this?
S. Dent: This is not right.
J. Charter: What do you mean?.
S. Dent: This whole project is wrong. We’re not helping anyone with this. It won’t be for medicine. We’re developing weapons.
J. Charter: I know. This is a military operation, as was stated in my briefing.
S. Dent: You knew? This whole time? They’re torturing people. Just so they can experiment on the survivors with this. You’re okay with that?
J. Charter: People suffer either way. Whether we complete this mission or not. You know that. We could be part of something great.
S. Dent: If we are building a future like this.. I want none of it.
J. Charter: You’re a traitor.
S. Dent: Please, think about it. We can escape this. Leave it behind. Knowing we won’t have innocent blood on our hands.
J. Charter: I trusted you, Cavil trusted you. Why would you sabotage the mission. We were going home. We were..
S. Dent: Cavil is preparing the escape pod. Please just come with me.
J. Charter: You all Lied to me. You betrayed me.
S. Dent: Please Julian, they are evil.
J. Charter: Why.
S. Dent: Julian, please. Calm down, Lower your weapon and join me. We’ll be okay.
S. Dent: Please calm down, Julian, please. Juli-.
J. Charter: I.. I’m sorry.

—----------------------- 23:13 - Central hallway

J. Charter: I’m sorry Sarah. I love you.

—----------------------- 23:16 - Cargo bay

J. Charter: I’m sorry.

The Pod

Text ⁠
Transcript security recording - Day 18
—----------------------- 00:23 - Pod-1

C. Darter: These might be the last words you’ll hear from me. Escape pods don’t have a great track record when it comes to landings.
C. Darter: Sarah is dead. The damn bastard shot her in the neck. Following orders before he launched himself out the airlock. Watched him sobbing through the hallway.
C. Darter: I didn’t want them to get hurt. It just happened.
C. Darter: She was innocent.
C. Darter: Sol, if you ever read the logs. I want you to know I’m not sorry for sabotaging your mission. You are a corrupt piece of shit who deserves to be put with the innocents you’re slaughtering.
C. Darter: I’ve got your documents. I’ve read your history. You were always like this.
C. Darter: Watch what happens when the common people figure out who you really are.
